M.A. Azim, Deputy Attorney General instructed by B. Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellant 
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent Nos. 1-3 
Respondent Nos. 4-7 ------ Not represented
parties:
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Patuakhali ------ Appellant
Vs.
Md. Nurul Haque & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
11. The learned Deputy Attorney General submits that the High court Division did not go into the merit of the matter. He further submits that Title Suit No. 54 of 1991 brought by the plaintiffs was not maintainable inasmuch as admittedly the suit land is khas land of the Government and the plaintiffs claim to have taken settlement of the same from the Government and the suit was brought for a decree for permanent injunction restraining the Government from creating any disturbance in the possession of the plaintiff by leasing out the suit land on yearly basis to any person and for further declaration that sheet No. 2 containing Plot Nos. 600-699 of Mouza Char Mominpur is forged, collusive and void. He next submits that since admittedly the suit land is khas land of the government and the same was leased is khas land of the government and the same was leased out to the plaintiffs on yearly basis, that suit itself for a decree for permanent injunction against the Government was not maintainable. He further submits that from the report of the Advocate Commissioner after local investigation it appears that sheet No.2 containing Plot Nos. 600-699 of Mouza Char Mominpur was genuine and the same did not overlap the suit land. He next submits that it is a fit case where this court can do complete justice by directing the trial court to accept the deposit of money as fee of Advocate Commissioner for the purpose of local investigation as ordered by the High Court Division although the deposit of money as commission fee was made beyond the time as fixed by the High Court Division in the peculiar facts and circumstances, of the present case also in view of the fact that the suit itself was not maintainable. 

 13. In. the facts and circumstances of the case and specially in view of the fact that the suit land is admittedly khas land of the Government and the plaintiffs are yearly lessees in respect of the same under the Government, the suit itself is not maintain-able for a decree for permanent injunction and, therefore, in the back ground of the facts of the instant case and as because question of law involved in the case needs resolution on trial, intervention of this court in the matter for doing complete justice to the parties in our view, would be quite appropriate and thereby parties would not be prejudiced, particularly plaintiffs since they accepted order of remand for fresh adjudication on surveying the land in suit and thus we are maintaining the order of the trial court accepting the deposit of money as commission fee made beyond the date fixed by the High Court Division as a special case. We are mindful of the fact that once time was fixed for depositing money as commission fee with a default clause and result thereof the same cannot be extended under section 148 of the Code of Civil Procedure but in the present case in view of the special circumstances as noted above, we took the above view for this case only. In sing so we are not departing from the principal that time cannot be extended in cases where time is fixed by the Court for doing an act with default clause followed by unequivocal result, i.e., there would be no requirement of further order for ensuring result of default. Accordingly the trial court is directed to take into consideration the commissioner's report as per law and any party to the suit may file objection against the commissioner's report within the time to be fixed by the trial court. The trial court thereafter would dispose of the suit in accordance with law.
